chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Isa from Safwan from Abu al-Mi'za from Sama'ah from Abu Basir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) married a woman, visited her, and intended to have intercourse with her, so he threw his cloak over her. Then he came to her. I said: 'Do you see that if he pays her full dowry, is it permissible for him to take back the cloak?' He said: 'No, for he made her private part permissible to him through it.'
ai.seo_question: Can a husband take back the cloak he threw over his wife after consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'istihlal' (making permissible) is applied to the physical act of intimacy, where the husband's cloak serves as a tangible symbol consummating the marital bond. This establishes that once the cloak is placed upon her to signify union, it becomes irrevocably linked to her private part, preventing its reclamation even upon payment of the full dowry. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the physical act of consummation solidifies the rights and obligations of the marriage contract beyond mere financial settlement.
